findings.title: Missing HIPAA BAA Flow-down
findings.deviation: The Contractor will perform data engineering on systems containing protected health information (PHI) but the agreement fails to incorporate a Business Associate Agreement (sub-BAA) or flow down HIPAA requirements as mandated by the Harrington BAA.
findings.impact: AtliQ will be out of compliance with its BAA with Harrington and HIPAA regulations if a subcontractor accesses PHI without a written back-to-back BAA.
findings.quote: The Parties have entered into, or will enter into, a Mutual Nondisclosure Agreement, which shall also apply.
findings.counterPosition: Require the Contractor to sign a Business Associate Agreement containing the same terms, conditions, and restrictions as Exhibit D of the Harrington Agreement prior to accessing any client systems or data.
findings.linkedQuote: In accordance with 45 C.F.R. §§ 164.502(e)(1)(ii) and 164.308(b)(2), Business Associate shall ensure that each Subcontractor agrees in writing, prior to any access to PHI, to the same restrictions, conditions and requirements that apply to Business Associate under this BAA.

findings.title: IP Assignment Conditioned on Payment
findings.deviation: Contractor's IP assignment is effective only 'upon payment' of the services, whereas Harrington requires immediate ownership of all Deliverables 'from creation' and irrevocable assignment 'without further consideration'.
findings.impact: If a payment dispute occurs, AtliQ cannot legally transfer the IP to Harrington as promised, creating conflict under the client contract.
findings.quote: To the extent any Work Product is not a work made for hire, the Contractor hereby assigns to the Company all right, title and interest in it, including all intellectual property rights, effective upon payment for the Services to which it relates.
findings.counterPosition: Revise the IP clause to assign all right, title, and interest immediately and unconditionally upon creation, removing the payment condition.
findings.linkedQuote: All Deliverables shall be deemed 'works made for hire' as defined in the U.S. Copyright Act, 17 U.S.C. § 101, and shall be the sole and exclusive property of Client from creation. To the extent any Deliverable... does not qualify as a work made for hire, Contractor hereby irrevocably assigns, transfers and conveys to Client all right, title and interest therein... without further consideration.

findings.title: Missing Background Checks and Training
findings.deviation: The agreement lacks any requirement for the Contractor to undergo the background checks, drug screenings, immunizations, and HIPAA compliance training mandated by the client.
findings.impact: AtliQ cannot permit the Contractor to access Harrington's systems or facilities without conflicting with the client's mandatory security rules.
findings.quote: Services | Data engineering: build and test ingestion pipelines from Harrington's electronic health record, patient accounting and scheduling systems into the cloud data platform; data quality checks; support for dashboard and readmission-model data preparation
findings.counterPosition: Insert a provision requiring the Contractor to successfully complete and pass all background checks, drug screenings, and HIPAA/compliance training required by Harrington prior to performing services.
findings.linkedQuote: Contractor Personnel accessing Client facilities or systems shall complete Client's background check, drug screening, immunization and compliance training requirements.

findings.title: Missing Offshore Data Restriction
findings.deviation: The agreement lists the Contractor's location as Austin, Texas but does not legally prohibit the Contractor from accessing or processing client PHI from outside the United States.
findings.impact: If the Contractor accesses Harrington's systems while traveling outside the US, AtliQ would be in direct conflict with Harrington's strict offshore restrictions.
findings.counterPosition: Add an explicit contractual restriction prohibiting the Contractor from accessing, viewing, storing, or processing any client PHI or other data from any location outside the United States.
findings.linkedQuote: Business Associate shall not, and shall ensure that no Subcontractor shall, access, view, create, receive, maintain, transmit, store or process PHI from or at any location outside the United States, whether directly or by remote access.

findings.title: Subcontract Requires Prior Client Consent
findings.deviation: Engaging Daniel Ortiz to perform services on Harrington's project is a subcontract, which requires Harrington's prior written consent, but the agreement does not address or condition itself on this requirement.
findings.impact: Engaging the contractor without Harrington's written approval conflicts with the client's prior consent requirements.
findings.quote: The Contractor may not assign or subcontract this Agreement without the Company's prior written consent.
findings.counterPosition: Confirm that Harrington has provided prior written consent for Daniel Ortiz, or make this agreement contingent upon obtaining such consent.
findings.linkedQuote: Contractor shall not subcontract any portion of the Services without Client's prior written consent.

fine.note: No delay penalties in the agreement, which matches the preferred standard.
Invoices are payable within 30 days of receipt, which is within the 45-day maximum.
Liability cap is mutual and limited to 1x fees paid/payable in the prior 12 months, with appropriate carve-outs.
Confidentiality obligations are mutual with a standard 3-year survival term.
Non-solicitation is mutual and limited to 6 months post-term, with no non-competes.
Notice period is mutual and payment upon termination is for all services performed up to the effective date.
Contractor's start date is after the client's contract was signed, meaning no early start risk.
